text.p: The Lietuva Hotel, the biggest in the country, said on Wednesday that its net profit in the first five months of the year dipped to 206,000 litas from 256,600 litas in the same period in 1996.
Chief finance officer Eugenija Krivoshejeva also told Reuters that the net profit of the firm in May rose to 622,000 litas from 147,000 litas in April.
"The tourist season is showing its effect and last month the hotel was operating at around 60 percent of its capacity," Krivoshejeva said.
The hotel said last month that it was operating at 26.8 percent capacity in April.
Krivoshejeva also said that the turnover of the hotel fell to 3.95 million litas in the first five months of the year from 4.25 million litas in the corresponding period in 1996.
The turnover in May was 1.33 million litas, she added.
"We expect that our monthly turnover will exceed one million litas each month until September," Krivoshejeva said.
The hotel reported a net profit of 817,000 litas in 1996.
The state-run Lietuva hotel has been slated for privatisation by the country's government but has attracted little interest from investors so far.
